entries.name: ModelsAPI
entries.doc:
Discover models and access their handles through ``session.models``.

``list_models`` lists available cards, and ``get_model`` loads a handle by
model identifier. Named properties provide handles for common models and
estimators for fitting SVD, UMAP and Gaussian process models.

members.name: get_model
members.doc:
Get a handle on a model by id.

A model with an accessor, named as its id with ``-`` as ``_``, gets the
accessor's handle. Other ids get their family's handle by prefix, or a
plain ``Model``.

Raises
------
ValueError
    If no system model has the id. A fitted model's id is checked when
    the handle is first used, since its fit may still be running.

entries.name: PoET2
entries.doc:
PoET-2, a multi-modal protein language model conditioned on a protein family.

Like PoET, every verb takes ``prompt``. Verbs other than ``indel`` also
take ``query``, a sequence, ``Protein``, ``Complex``, ``Query`` or query id,
sent as ``query_id``, which conditions on a protein's sequence or
structure. Its checkpoint is ``poet-2``.

``fold`` takes a sequence, ``Protein``, ``Complex``, a list of these, or

``complexes``. Chains outside the card's ``input_types`` are left out,
and a card that isn't ``multichain`` folds one protein per complex.
MSAs and templates, given as ``templates`` or attached to the inputs,
are sent where the model's params take them.

----------
n_splits : int, optional
    Number of random folds, between 2 and 10 (default 5). Keeps rows sharing a
    sequence in the same fold. Mutually exclusive with ``folds``.
folds : sequence of int, optional
    Test fold of each row of the training assay, one entry per row in assay
    order, labelled 0..K-1 with none empty and 2 <= K <= 10. Rows are assigned
    independently of which sequence they hold, unlike ``n_splits``. Use -1 to
    exclude a row, which then comes back with a fold of -1 and NaN predictions.
    Splitting a repeated sequence across folds leaks, since embeddings come
    from the sequence, so expect optimistic scores.
